dialog.body: Public Works, this is Kevin. How can I help you?
Hello, Kevin. Yes, good morning. My name is Marco Ricci. I am calling about the water on my street, from the drain. Sorry, I am in a parking garage, so there is an echo. Nobody is here, it is empty.
No problem, I can hear you fine. Echo and all. What's the address?
It is eighty-one Old Beach Road. On the Easton's Beach side, near the end where you go toward the water.
Okay, eighty-one Old Beach Road. And what's going on there?

So, after the rain on Friday into Saturday, three days ago, the water came down the hill from the next street. It runs down, and it goes straight into my yard. Straight in. And this is not new, it happens every time we have a heavy rain.
Mm-hm. Water coming down off the hill, into the yard. Got it. Is it getting to the house, or just the yard?

The yard, mostly, it is standing there. And the sidewalk, it is a sheet of mud and grit. All the sand and the stones come down with the water. You cannot walk there without slipping. My neighbor, she almost fell on Sunday.

Yeah, that grit is no good. Let me write this down. Sidewalk covered in mud and grit, runoff from the upper street into the yard. [pause] Is there a storm drain near you that's clogged, or is it more that there isn't one catching it?

[pause] I think there is one, at the corner, but it is full of the same grit. The water goes past it. So it does not take the water. Nobody cleans it, I think. I have called before about this kind of thing, and nobody came.
Okay. I don't have the earlier notes in front of me, so I'll put this in fresh. Can I ask you something, though?
Yes, of course.
Do you know which street the hill runoff is coming from? The cross street up above you?
I do not know the name exactly. It is the street above, the one that goes up behind the houses. Sorry. I can send a picture, if you want.
That's all right, we'll find it from your address. Landmarks help too, so that's good.

Okay. And I want to ask, because I do not understand this. Is it a city drain or a state one? Someone told me some roads here belong to the state, and then the city says it is not theirs. I do not want to wait again and then hear it is the wrong office.

Fair question. Honestly, it depends on the road. Most of the drains on city streets are ours, but a few roads in town are state-owned, and the drains on those are the state's. I can't tell you for sure on yours just from the name. What I'll do is send a crew to look at it, and if it turns out to be state, we pass it to them ourselves. You won't have to chase it.
That is good. That is what I want. Because it keeps happening, and every time it is the same. Rain, then the mud, then the yard. I am tired of it, honestly.

I hear you. Rain on Friday, still a mess on Tuesday, that's a long time with grit on a sidewalk. I'm putting it down as a drain blockage and a sidewalk hazard, both. That should get it looked at sooner.
Thank you. When will somebody come? Do you know?
Crews are working through a pile of calls from that storm. I'd say sometime this week, with the sidewalk part likely first. Can I get a number in case they need to reach you?
Yes. It is four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-seven-six.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-six. Under Marco Ricci, eighty-one Old Beach Road. Did I spell Ricci right? R-I-C-C-I?
Yes, that is right. Two C's.
Perfect. Anything else you want me to add? Like how deep the water gets in the yard?
It is a few inches, near the fence side, and it takes a day to go down. That is all. Just please, someone should come and look at the drain at the corner.
Got it, a few inches, takes a day to drain. All in the notes. You'll get a call if they need anything.
Thank you, Kevin. I appreciate your help. God bless you, and have a good day.
You too, Marco. Take care, and watch your step on that sidewalk.
